chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Rafa'ah al-Nakhhas, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'The Romans raid the Saqaliba and steal their children, both slave-girls and slave-boys. They take the boys, castrate them, and then send them to Baghdad to the merchants. What do you think regarding buying them, knowing that they have been stolen, and they were raided not in a war that was between them?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no harm in buying them; they are taken out of polytheism and brought into the house of Islam.'

key_terms.الرُّومَ: The Romans (Byzantines), referring to the dominant non-Muslim power of the era.
key_terms.الشِّرْكِ: Polytheism, referring to the state of non-Muslims before entering Islam.
key_terms.الصَّقَالِبَةِ: Saqaliba, a term used for Slavic or European peoples, often used for slaves in this context.
key_terms.دَارِ الْإِسْلَامِ: The house of Islam, referring to the realm where Islamic law prevails.

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy slaves who were stolen from non-Muslim lands without a formal war?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that the permissibility of purchasing these slaves rests on their transition from *Dar al-Shirk* (land of polytheism) to *Dar al-Islam* (land of Islam), rendering the lack of formal war (*ghazw*) irrelevant to their legal status. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle that the primary determinant for the validity of ownership is the change in religious domicile rather than the military context of capture, a nuance often debated in *fiqh* regarding *al-masaqit* (those captured without battle).

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Rafa’at Al Nakhhas who said,

‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The Romans are invading upon Al-Saqaliba (between Turkey and Bulgaria). So they are stealing their children, from the slave-girls and the slave-boys. So they are deliberating to the boys and castrating them, then they are sending them to Baghdad to the merchants. So what is your<sup>asws</sup> view regarding buying them, and we know that they have been stolen, but rather they were invaded upon from other than a war which was between them’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It not unlawful to buy them as they are taken out of the Polytheism and (brought) into the house of Al-Islam’.
en.sarwar: 9. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad all from ibn Mahbub from Rifa’ah al- Nakhkhas who has said the following:

“I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about Romans who invade al-Saqalibah (a people who lived between Bulgaria and Constantinople (Istanbul)), steal their children, slave-girls and slave-boys, then castrate the slave-boys, then send them to Baghdad for the merchants. What do you say about them and we know they are stolen and they were invaded wrongfully without declared war among them. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful to buy them because they have only taken them from paganism to al-Islam.’”
